purpose: Solve scalar and physical-length tensor AQUAL on all nominal registered baryonic maps, testing convergence and domain-selective field response without opening a velocity or lensing target.
source_construction: Phi_N is the zero-padded baryonic thin-sheet Newtonian potential; applying the same variational isotropic graph operator to Phi_N supplies a dimensionally consistent projected source, and the observed Phi_N boundary is held fixed.

definitions.sigma: P0662 physical tidal-length quadratic tensor coefficient
definitions.scalar_control: the identical nonlinear solve with sigma=0
definitions.tensor_effect: RMS vector acceleration difference between tensor and scalar solves divided by scalar RMS acceleration in the central 80-percent-width square

solver.boundary: baryonic thin-sheet Newtonian potential on the outermost cells

selection_rule: The tensor field law advances to spent-outcome topology only if every solver, conservation, galaxy-preservation, cluster-response, domain-ratio, parameter, and blindness gate passes. No failed threshold may be relaxed.
claim_boundary: P0664 establishes numerical field behavior on projected baryonic maps only; it does not compare with velocities or lensing constraints.

The projected source construction is dimensionally consistent and recovers the thin-sheet Newtonian potential in its constant-mu scalar limit, but it is not a three-dimensional or covariant derivation.
A domain-selective field response is necessary but not sufficient for galaxy-plus-cluster unification.
No P0633 velocity, P0640 lens constraint, or spent lens residual may be used in P0664 development or selection.
